Lessons.Title: Reasoning about Angles (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will the purpose of this lesson is twofold: for you to use known angles to reason about unknown angles on a clock, and for them to practice drawing angles of given measurements.
Angles are ever present on an analog clock. In this lesson, you investigate and solve problems about the angles formed by a clock’s hour and minute hands. You reason about the number of degrees between the two hands or the number of degrees the minute hand has turned over some specified time.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Time After Time (10 minutes); Activity 1: Draw a Clock (15 minutes); Activity 2: Tick Tock (20 minutes); Cool-down: One Angle at a Time (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Use a clock as a 360° circle with 12 equal 30° sectors; construct angles from known positions and turns.

Edulytics authored guidance: Draw perpendicular vertical and horizontal diameters to locate 12, 3, 6 and 9. Divide each quadrant into three equal 30° clock sectors. At exactly 4:00, four sectors between 12 and 4 produce a 120° smaller angle.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): What is the smaller angle at exactly 4:00? Show clock-sector reasoning.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
